newsitem.title: USA: TVA sets more cost cuts to offset warmth.
newsitem.headline: TVA sets more cost cuts to offset warmth.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority said Thursday it is initiating additional cost-cutting steps to offset the impact of a mild winter that resulted in lower-than-projected power revenues.

The cost reductions include eliminating a portion of TVA's fleet of vehicles, reducing travel expenses, cutting discretionary expenses, delaying equipment purchases and not filling non-critical personnel positions.
The additional cost-cutting actions are expected to save about $30 million in the year ending September 30, it said.
"These reductions coupled with a hot summer could put us back on budget," Chief Financial Officer David Smith said.

Smith said warmer-than-normal winter temperatures have resulted in a decrease of 1.2 billion kilowatt hours in current year sales to TVA municipal and cooperative distributors compared to the first five months of last year.
He said February sales alone were down 10 percent from last year.

In cutting vehicle costs, TVA said, it will increase the mileage rate for employees to encourage the use of personal cars, request bids to replace a portion of TVA's fleet with rental vehicles and reduce the number of work vehicles assigned to organizations by 20 percent.
TVA has reduced expenses more than $800 million a year during the last several years as part of a continuing effort to remain competitive.
"These extra cost-cutting efforts not only will help our cash flow this year, but also will continue to help TVA compete effectively in the future," Smith said.
